registered_revision: recorded by the commit that first adds this file; the commit is before any screen, rollout, interpolation or score named here
purpose: Register the revised stage 2 on-policy recipe before any score: student-policy rollouts with an 8-sample pass-rate estimate and p(1-p) problem weighting, a separate 2B teacher scoring pass over the student's own tokens, a verified-answer reward gate on reverse-KL supervision, loop-onset relay continuations, rank-64 all-linear LoRA merged at the end, a learning rate selected by the fixed-batch KL gate near 10x the full-fine-tuning rate, and a 0.5M/1M/2M/5M scoring cadence. The win bar is unchanged from the stage-1 registration; the retention sample is enlarged because 504 MMLU-Pro items cannot resolve a 1.0-point bound.

stage2a.result: not a win: GSM8K +2.88 points with an interval barely above zero, MATH-500 -11.0 points with the interval entirely below zero, MMLU -1.94 points outside the retention bound
stage2a.relation: this registration changes the objective, the parameterisation and the cadence in response to a measured failure. It does not rewrite the S58 report or the S55/S56 amendments; it supersedes only the stage-2b training and cadence clauses named in `supersedes`.

stage2b_v1.relation: keeps the sampling policy, verifier, loop cut, dedup rule, hold-out exclusion, three-arm attribution and win bar; replaces the full-fine-tune + completion-CE recipe with the on-policy reverse-KL recipe below

win_basis.relation: the student, the evaluation instrument and the paired problem-level statistics are unchanged

supersedes: stage2b_v1.training.arm: 'full text tower' -> rank-64 all-linear LoRA, merged
stage2b_v1.training.objective: completion CE -> reward-gated reverse KL plus loop-onset relay
stage2b_v1.training.lr: one screened rate -> the fixed-batch KL gate starting at 1e-4
stage2b_v1.win_bar.retention_note: 504 MMLU-Pro items -> a sample large enough, or an explicit unresolved label

student.identity_check: oracle/frontier/identity.py against models/FRONTIER-POST-TRAINED.lock.json before load; id, revision, snapshot directory name, first-shard weight sha256 and licence sha256; mismatch fails closed
student.mode: non-thinking, the policy's own tokenizer and chat template
student.active_union_reading: rank-64 LoRA leaves the deployed model a full-weight text tower; after the adapter is merged there are no extra deployed identities, so the unique active union is still 752,393,024

rollouts.prompts: GSM8K-train and MATH-train items with an extractable train label, seeded stratified over (source, difficulty, reasoning-length quartile), minus every id in results/artifacts/stage2/s58-combined/stage2a-combined-holdout.jsonl and minus any prompt used by the interpolation calibration split
rollouts.stop: EOS only; a rollout that reaches the cap without EOS is counted truncated and is not a verified target
rollouts.pass_rate: p = verified-correct samples / K per problem, K=8; p is the empirical pass rate and is never inferred from the teacher
rollouts.loss_weight: w(p) = p(1-p) per problem, the PACED weighting; problems with p in {0, 1} carry w=0 and are counted, not silently dropped
rollouts.unit: difficulty-weighted step: the step objective is sum_i w_i * sum_t KL_i,t / sum_i w_i * n_i, where n_i is the supervised token count of rollout i. This is the explicit third unit of learning (example, token, difficulty-weighted step) and is not the SFT trainer's token unit

teacher_pass.access: separate pass, after the rollout pass has exited; the student and teacher are never co-resident on the device
teacher_pass.conditioning: the teacher consumes the student's own sampled token ids (same-prefix contract); a shape or id mismatch fails closed
teacher_pass.output: one log-probability per sampled token (scalar per token), no top-k cache; at bf16 that is 4 bytes per token, ~4 MB per million tokens
teacher_pass.storage_arithmetic: a 12M-token pass writes ~48 MB of log-probabilities, versus gigabytes for a top-k cache; the receipt records the realised bytes
teacher_pass.objective: reverse KL(student_T || teacher_T) at T=2.0 on the sampled completion tokens; prompt positions contribute neither CE nor KL
teacher_pass.reward_gate: only rollouts whose final answer verifies against the train label (frontier.rft.verify == correct) contribute to the reverse-KL loss; the gate is the verified final answer, not a teacher likelihood

loop_onset_relay.trigger: a rollout that reached the cap or was classified as a loop by oracle/frontier/termination.py
loop_onset_relay.cut: cut at the recorded loop onset (the first token of the first repeated block), keeping the student's prefix
loop_onset_relay.handoff: the 2B teacher continues autoregressively from the student's own cut prefix, in the same separate pass
loop_onset_relay.admission: only a relay continuation whose final answer verifies against the train label is kept; a relay that does not verify contributes nothing
loop_onset_relay.supervision: reverse KL(student_T || teacher_T) on the relay tokens, at the student's own prefix; the student's pre-cut tokens are not re-supervised
loop_onset_relay.counted: relay attempts, verified relays, rejected relays and relay tokens are receipted separately from ordinary rollouts
loop_onset_relay.literature_position: OLIVE (arXiv:2609.36246) supports teacher continuation from the student's prefix but trains by cross-entropy on teacher tokens, not reverse KL; Relay-OPD (arXiv:2607.26057) supports a teacher handoff but triggers on a failed-prefix asymmetry, not a loop detector. The reverse-KL-on-relay-tokens combination is this registration's hypothesis, not a published result (docs/S60-LITERATURE.md).

parameterisation.adapter: LoRA rank 64 on every linear layer (attention q/k/v/o and MLP/MoE gate/up/down), alpha 32, the 1/r scaling already implied by alpha/r; zero-initialised B and uniform A as in the PEFT default
parameterisation.why_all_linear: LoRA Without Regret (Thinking Machines, 2025-09-29) finds attention-only LoRA underperforms MLP-only and all-layer LoRA matches full fine-tuning; rank 64 is inside its 1-512 sweep
parameterisation.merge: the adapter is merged into the base weights at the end; the deployed checkpoint is a full-weight model, and the active union is unchanged at 752,393,024
parameterisation.not_frozen: the tied embedding is part of the base and is not adapted by an MLP/attention LoRA; the merged model still reads all 752,393,024 text-tower elements

learning_rate_gate.basis: 10x the full-fine-tuning rate (1e-5) that stage 2a used; LoRA Without Regret measures the optimal LoRA LR at ~10x the FullFT LR, and the registration starts there rather than assuming it
learning_rate_gate.instrument: the S50 fixed-batch KL gate: the same fixed batch, the same teacher, the KL at 2M processed tokens
learning_rate_gate.decision_rule: choose the largest screened rate whose fixed-batch KL is below the gate threshold recorded by the S50 receipt; if every rate rises, the run does not launch and the screen is reported. Accuracy is not the selection input at the screen
learning_rate_gate.recorded: the chosen rate, every screened rate's KL, the fixed-batch hash and the threshold are written before the full run

training.objective: difficulty-weighted reward-gated reverse KL plus loop-onset relay reverse KL
training.budget: the corpus is one pass over the student's rollouts; the cadence is expressed in processed student tokens
training.seq_len: the rollout length distribution measured by the pilot, capped at 2048
training.micro_batch_and_accum: chosen from the measured memory peak; the loss unit is the difficulty-weighted step, so the micro-batch partition does not change the objective
training.checkpoint_every: every 0.5M processed tokens, so the 0.5M / 1M / 2M / 5M points are exact
training.optimizer: Adam8bit block 256, int8 first moment, bf16 second moment, stochastic weight rounding
training.no_teacher_at_training: the teacher log-probabilities are read from the separate pass; no teacher weights are loaded during student training
training.unregistered_deviation_rule: any change to these knobs is a new registered amendment before the launch

scoring_cadence.instrument: scripts/s54_post_trained_eval.py; full GSM8K (1319) and MATH-500 (500), greedy, non-thinking, zero-shot with \boxed{}, batch 32, cap 4096, three extraction bases side by side
scoring_cadence.diagnostics: termination, truncation and loop rates at every point, from the receipt's own summary
scoring_cadence.retention: MMLU (14,042 items) and MMLU-Pro on a 4,000-item total-cap subset at every point; the 504-item MMLU-Pro sample is retired as a retention instrument because its paired interval cannot resolve the 1.0-point bound
scoring_cadence.why_four_points: S58 found the 2M checkpoint collapsed to 0.3101 GSM8K and recovered monotonically; a 0.5M point makes the early transient visible instead of inferred

retention.bound: MMLU and MMLU-Pro each stay within 1.0 point: point drop <= 1.0 and the paired interval lower bound >= -1.0
retention.mmul_pro_basis: a seeded total-cap subset of the MMLU-Pro test items, allocated by the S43 largest-remainder rule; the subset and its seed are recorded before the first score
retention.uncertainty_treatment: if the paired interval lower bound is below -1.0 while the point estimate is inside 1.0, the clause is reported as `unresolved`, not as a pass; an unresolved retention clause blocks a win claim but does not by itself count as a retention failure
retention.why_not_504: 504 items give a paired interval of roughly +/-4 points at the observed base accuracy, so the S58 claim could not resolve the bound it tested; the larger sample is the fix

win_bar.statement: the arm wins iff (1) greedy GSM8K flexible > 0.5421 AND greedy MATH-500 flexible > 0.3820, with the prompt-level (problem-level) paired 95% interval of each difference entirely above zero, AND (2) the retention bound above holds for both MMLU and MMLU-Pro
win_bar.no_softening: a gain on one task, a maj@16-only gain, a gain shared with the matched control, or an accuracy gain with an unresolved retention clause is not the win
win_bar.statistics: problem-level paired bootstrap, 4,000 resamples, seed 53, against the post-trained 0.8B; the resampling unit is the problem, never the token
win_bar.unchanged_from: docs/ws19-post-trained-route-registration-v1.json; S58 measured 0.5421 and 0.3820 as the bar

attribution.matched_control: the same rollouts, budget, optimiser, LoRA rank, LR and cadence with the reward gate off (every sampled rollout, verified or not); the difference isolates the verified-answer gate
attribution.relay_control: the same rollouts and gate with relay disabled; the difference isolates the loop-onset relay
attribution.not_a_win_condition: both controls are reported with their own paired intervals and do not change the win bar

limits.container_memory: sized from the measured peak of each phase (rollout, teacher scoring, training) by max(1.5 x peak, peak + 1 GiB), recorded before the launch
limits.vram: sized from the same measured peak; a phase whose measured peak is 10.9 GiB must not inherit an 8 GiB limit
limits.host_reservation: host MemAvailable must exceed the new limit plus 4 GiB before launch; a serialized second job must not start while its limit plus the running job's measured peak exceeds available memory
limits.bounded_tmp: SELVEDGE_TMP is 2g or the phase-specific measured need, whichever is larger

what_this_file_does_not_establish: that p(1-p) weighting improves this student: PACED supports the weighting in its own setting, the screen is the test here
that loop-onset relay improves over no relay: the relay control is the test
that reverse KL on relay tokens is supported by OLIVE: OLIVE trains by cross-entropy on teacher tokens
that rank-64 all-linear LoRA matches full fine-tuning here: LoRA Without Regret supports the regime, this run measures it
that the 4,000-item MMLU-Pro subset resolves 1.0 point: its interval is reported, and an unresolved clause is labelled as such
any score: nothing in this file is a measurement
